hilfe: Ores that are not in data/erze.json at all.
The game rolls them up while you play: name, look, value, rarity, from
which level they lie in the ground, what you can make out of them - and
whether they can be alloyed. The first time you mine such an ore it gets
its own page in the wiki, just like any other.
IT NEVER ENDS
At the start there are only the ores from data/erze.json - Stone, Coal,
Copper up to Diamond. From "ab_level" on, ONE new ore is added every
"je_level" levels, forever. How rare it is comes out of the level it is
born in: level 40 brings something far beyond Diamond. There is no end to
the ladder.
ROLLED ONCE, FIXED FOREVER
A finished ore goes into the save file with everything that makes it up.
If you change the word lists or the curves here later, the ores that
already exist stay exactly as they are - only the next ones look
different. It MUST be that way: your bag only stores the NUMBER of an ore.
"startwert" is the die for a NEW game. Each ore derives its own die from
it plus its running number - so the same start value gives the same series
again.
WHY NOTHING CAN GET TOO STRONG
Only ONE number is rolled per ore: the rarity, and that comes from the
level. Everything else hangs off it - value, mining time and from which
level it lies in the ground. An ore that is in front of you all the time
therefore cannot be the most expensive one. The formulas below are the
same curves the ores from data/erze.json follow (Stone 1 money, Diamond
"seltenheit.streuung" is the only randomness in it: 0.35 means an ore may
be up to 35 percent rarer or more common than its level says. Without it a
boring straight series would come out.
THE NAMES
A name is put together from 2 to 4 words, always by the same blueprint -
that is why they always fit together:
vorne  [mitte]  CORE  [hinten]
Ember  -        quartz -      ->  Ember Quartz         (2)
Frost  -        ore    shard  ->  Frost Ore Shard      (3)
Night  ash      stone  vein   ->  Night Ash Stone Vein (4)
The CORE word comes from the kind (below), so that a metal is called like
a metal and a crystal like a crystal. Every word is capitalised and joined
with a space.
THE KINDS
A kind decides what an ore looks like and what you may do with it.
name        only for messages.
kern        the core words for the name.
zustaende   like "zustaende" in data/erze.json. "raw" is always added.
farbton     range on the colour wheel, 0-360 (0 red, 120 green, 240 blue).
Both colours of an ore get the same hue and differ only in
brightness - that is why they always match.
sattheit    how strong the colour is, 0 grey to 1 vivid.
muster      how fine the veins are (like "muster" in data/erze.json).
reinheit    range for the starting purity in percent.
gewicht     how often this kind is drawn.
ALLOYING
Ores of a kind with "legieren": true can get a recipe with another such
ore - then an additional new material comes into being, exactly like in
data/legierungen.json. "legierung.anteil" says how many of the rolled ores
get one (0 = none, 1 = all that fit).
The partner must be smeltable AND alloyable - so only metals qualify, from
data/erze.json just as well as rolled ones.
ORDER
The rolled ores hang at the BACK of the list, after everything from
data/erze.json and data/legierungen.json. That way the numbers of the
hand-written ores stay valid.
